What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
q-115292.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(-6,-5),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=3.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-6))^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-5))^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+6)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y+5)^{2}}{9} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-7623.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(2,1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=4,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-115286.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(-4,3),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=4,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

q-16554.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(2,1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=2,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=4.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{{4}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{16} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
